content: The symptoms of Middle East Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus (MERS-CoV) infection typically include fever, cough, shortness of breath, and gastrointestinal symptoms such as diarrhea and vomiting. Fever and pneumonia of unknown etiology that require hospitalization should prompt evaluation for MERS-CoV in consultation with state and local health departments. The most common symptoms observed in patients with MERS-CoV infection are as follows: Fever, reported in 98% of cases. Cough, observed in 83% of cases. Shortness of breath, present in 72% of cases. Gastrointestinal symptoms, including diarrhea in 26% of cases and vomiting in 21% of cases. Among patients with MERS-CoV infection, 96% had at least one chronic medical condition. The most frequently reported comorbidities include: Diabetes, present in 68% of cases. Hypertension, observed in 34% of cases. Heart disease, reported in 28% of cases. Kidney disease, present in 49% of cases. Additionally, 72% of patients had more than one chronic medical condition. In a retrospective study involving 47 patients diagnosed with MERS-CoV infection, 89% (42 patients) required intensive care, and 72% (34 patients) required mechanical ventilation.
